principle_text: When the persuadee shares personal experiences related to your topic, you should build rapport by sharing your own similar experiences before introducing the charitable cause.
When the persuadee acknowledges information without showing clear interest, avoid only providing facts without connecting emotionally or addressing their underlying curiosity.
When the persuadee shares a personal challenge or vulnerability, avoid shifting the focus away from their experience with unrelated lighthearted comments.

When the persuadee responds with casual, personal remarks that do not relate to the charitable cause, avoid making neutral or purely personal statements that do not guide the conversation toward donation or cause engagement.
When the persuadee shows casual interest in your conversation, you should smoothly introduce the charity to prompt curiosity and encourage engagement.
When the persuadee responds with a personal belief unrelated to donation intent, avoid assuming informational statements alone will increase willingness to donate.
When the persuadee shows initial awareness and tentative willingness to donate, you should introduce the charity’s urgent needs clearly to encourage positive engagement and move toward commitment.
When the persuadee expresses ambivalence about their own virtues but shows openness, you should introduce a reputable charity clearly and positively to encourage their interest and engagement.
When the persuadee shares personal information without showing increased engagement, avoid shifting focus away from connecting the issue to their values or emotions.
When the persuadee shares personal information related to family, avoid shifting the conversation away from the charitable cause without linking it back to the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows recognition but no clear interest in the charity, avoid assuming prior involvement will motivate immediate donation commitment.

When the persuadee shares relevant personal involvement in charitable activities, avoid shifting the focus to unrelated personal anecdotes that do not directly connect to the cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee expresses skepticism about how donations are used, avoid ignoring or overlooking their concerns about donation transparency and impact.
When the persuadee focuses on personal topics unrelated to the charity, avoid responses that do not gently steer the conversation back to the donation goal.
When the persuadee shares personal experiences unrelated to the charity, avoid focusing only on empathy without steering the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses neutrality or uncertainty about the discussion topic, avoid vague or unrelated statements that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee is already familiar with and actively supports a charity, avoid simply naming the charity without adding new, compelling information or reasons to deepen their engagement.
When the persuadee expresses empathy or concern about the cause, you should make a direct and heartfelt plea linking their emotions to a specific, actionable donation request.

When the persuadee shows only mild recognition of a charity and requests more information, avoid assuming immediate interest or pushing for a donation without providing clear, compelling details about the organization's impact.

When the persuadee indicates they did not personally experience the hardships being discussed, avoid assuming shared experiences and instead acknowledge their perspective before connecting to the cause.
When the persuadee shares personal involvement in volunteering without indicating donation interest, avoid focusing solely on their experience without gently steering toward the donation topic.
When the persuadee expresses personal discomfort without mentioning the charitable cause, avoid focusing solely on empathy without gently steering the conversation toward the donation topic.
When the persuadee shows signs of discomfort or distraction, you should gently acknowledge their state and politely ask for permission to discuss the charitable cause to foster openness.
When the persuadee shares a personal experience of hardship related to poverty, avoid dismissing or minimizing their feelings and instead acknowledge their emotions sincerely.
When the persuadee shows awareness of an issue without expressing donation intent, avoid only confirming their knowledge without linking it to a call for action or donation motivation.

When the persuadee shows only neutral recognition of a charity without expressing commitment, avoid asking questions that merely confirm legitimacy without linking to emotional engagement or donation motivation.
When the persuadee expresses wariness about donating due to mistrust of organizations, avoid immediately asking about past donations without addressing their concerns first.
When the persuadee expresses concern but shifts focus to external solutions, avoid only describing the problem without connecting it to how the listener can personally help.
When the persuadee relates personally to the issue through shared experiences, you should express your own similar experiences and feelings to build empathy and deepen emotional engagement.
When the persuadee shows interest but lacks information about the charity, avoid giving vague or minimal details that do not clearly connect to a donation appeal.
When the persuadee responds with conditional or non-committal statements, avoid asking overly broad or abstract questions that do not guide them toward a specific stance on donating.

When the persuadee expresses conditional or uncertain support, you should personalize the cause by highlighting specific vulnerable groups to increase emotional engagement and positive acknowledgment.
When the persuadee shows familiarity with a charitable organization, avoid asking simple recognition questions that do not deepen engagement or move toward commitment.
When the persuadee expresses sadness and a desire to help, you should introduce serious, relatable issues that evoke empathy and increase their engagement with the cause.
When the persuadee shares personal challenges, you should express empathy and relate with your own experiences to build rapport and increase their willingness to engage with the donation topic.

When the persuadee expresses a preference for supporting local charities, avoid immediately requesting donations to broader or less familiar organizations without first acknowledging their preference.
When the persuadee expresses openness but lacks knowledge about a cause, you should introduce the charity by name to engage their curiosity and invite them to learn more.
When the persuadee expresses empathy or emotional engagement with a hardship, you should highlight personal contrasts to deepen their emotional connection and motivate charitable consideration.
